subject: Post-demo pricing: prefix cache assumptions & budget alignment
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@finteq.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finteq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: prefix cache assumptions & budget alignment

Hi Sarah / Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation and helpful context on FinteQ's payment flows. Quick written recap of what we captured + a couple of clarifying asks so Ben and I can lock down numbers for the pricing worksheet.

Key points from the call:
- Expected volume: 8–12M total tokens / month initially (peak month) with growth to ~25M over 12 months.
- Prompt profile: about 65% of calls are short (50–150 tokens output), 35% are longer (400–1,200 tokens) tied to dispute summaries and reconciliation prompts.
- Latency target: 200–300ms p50 for short prompts; longer prompts can be 1.5–2s.
- Primary ask: provide target effective cost per 1M tokens (after caching) that fits within FinteQ's $30–$50k monthly budget for model serving.

Caching assumptions we discussed (please confirm):
1) Prefix (session) cache will capture repeated framing tokens + system prompt & user metadata for conversational flows — most effective on short prompts.
2) Cache warm state: we should assume a 10% cold fraction for session initialization across users.
3) Expected steady-state prefix cache hit range: 30%–45% for your live traffic (your engineering estimate was ~35%).
4) Cache TTL: active sessions kept in KV for 12–24 hours, then evicted unless re-accessed.

What I need from you to finalize the sheet:
- Confirm whether 8–12M tokens/month is the right starting window (a single number helps us present three price tiers).
- Reconfirm your target effective $/1M tokens post-caching (you mentioned wanting something that keeps monthly spend under $50k).

Next steps: Ben will attach a quick model showing how different hit rates move the effective $/1M token metric. I’ll also draft an SOW with the Dedicated capacity sizing options so procurement has a place to start.

If this looks right I’ll send a follow-up with two price scenarios (conservative and aggressive cache assumptions) and a recommended starter commit. Are you available for a 30-minute follow-up on Wednesday (Apr 28) to review the sheet?

Best,
Laura Bennett

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah@finteq.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finteq.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: prefix cache assumptions & budget alignment

Laura / Sarah / Daniel —

Following up with the quick math (sheet attached: prefix-cache-model.xlsx). Below is a short explainer and one worked example so everyone has the same baseline.

Assumptions (base model):
- Baseline model compute list price: $1,200 per 1M tokens (this is the per-token compute cost before applying cache reductions).
- Cache hit reduction: when a token can be served from prefix/KV cache we assume its incremental compute cost is 10% of baseline (small memory lookup + emission vs full attention compute).
- Storage/serving cost for cache: $80 / 1M tokens served from cache (includes memory and cross-server reads amortized).
- Cold fraction: 10% of requests are cold (no cache) and pay full baseline.

Worked example (8M tokens / month):
- Hit rate = 35% (steady).
- Cold = 10% of traffic (assumed uniformly distributed).
- Effective untouched traffic (hits excluded): 8M * (1 - 0.35) = 5.2M tokens that require full or partial compute.
- Of that 5.2M, cold fraction pays full baseline: 5.2M * 0.10 = 0.52M tokens * $1,200 = $624k.
- Cache-hit tokens (2.8M) pay cache-serve cost: 2.8M * $80 = $224k plus incremental compute for cache hits: 2.8M * ($1,200 * 0.10) = $336k.
- Remaining warm-but-not-cached tokens pay full compute: (5.2M - 0.52M - 2.8M) = -0.12M (edge rounding) — in practice warm-not-cached is small; adjust with sheet.

Total monthly cost (approx) = $624k (cold full) + $336k (hit incremental compute) + $224k (cache storage) = $1.184M for 8M tokens.

Effective $/1M tokens = $1.184M / 8 = $148k per 1M tokens (this is an illustrative number with the baseline assumptions above).

Notes:
- This example shows how sensitive the effective $/1M token number is to the baseline compute price and cache hit fraction. If we use a different baseline (e.g., a quantized model at $400 / 1M tokens) the final effective metric drops dramatically.
- The sheet includes toggles for baseline model selection (full, quantized, reranked) and hit-rate sweeps (25%–55%).

Action requested from FinteQ: pick your preferred baseline model tier and confirm the hit-rate expectation (35% used here). With that I’ll generate two scenarios that map to your $30–$50k / month budget target so procurement can see commit levels.

I’ll sync with Laura to bundle this into an SOW draft.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: prefix-cache-model.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: sanity-check on FinteQ assumptions

Quick internal note — Laura / Ben, a couple of adjustments I recommend before we finalize numbers for the external sheet: 

1) Baseline model: don’t use the $1,200 / 1M tokens as the default for all scenarios. Offer two baseline tiers: "standard" at $420 / 1M and "high-accuracy" at $1,200 / 1M. Show both side-by-side.
2) Cache incremental compute: 10% of baseline is reasonable for short-token emit paths. Flag a sensitivity where incremental compute is 20% to cover less-optimized code paths.
3) Hit-rate buckets: present Low/Medium/High = 25% / 35% / 50% rather than a single point estimate. FinteQ’s engineers should see the tradeoffs.

I updated the attached SOW-draft.pdf with a recommended starter commit (3-month) and a clause for a hit-rate review at month 2 to rebase pricing if actual traffic diverges by >20%.

If you want I can join the Wed follow-up to walk procurement through the SOW clauses.

-MK
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachment: SOW-draft.pdf

Sarah / Daniel —

Thanks — summarizing next steps and the numbers we’ll surface in Wednesday’s follow-up: 

1) We’ll deliver two pricing scenarios by EOD Tuesday:
   - Conservative: baseline = $1,200 / 1M, hit-rate sweep (25% / 35% / 50%).
   - Optimized: baseline = $420 / 1M (quantized model), hit-rate sweep (25% / 35% / 50%).
2) We’ll show effective $/1M tokens for each cell in the matrix (sheet attached). The primary lever to get within your $30–$50k/month target is: a) pick the quantized model AND b) reach at least 35% prefix hit rate.
3) We propose a 3-month starter commit (see SOW-draft.pdf) with a month-2 hit-rate review and an adjustment clause if actual hit rate is >20% different from the estimate.
4) Requested from FinteQ: please confirm a starting monthly token number (8M / 10M / 12M). If you prefer, tell us a single expected month (e.g., 10M) and we’ll bake that into the scenarios.

Proposed follow-up: Wed Apr 28, 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include Ben + Markus to go through the sheet live.

Best,
